title: Implement a circuit-breaker state machine
statement:
Step 10 · Failure control

A circuit breaker stops calling a failing dependency for a cooldown, then permits a recovery probe. Here calls complete synchronously before the next event, so only one probe is in flight. Production concurrency requires an atomic half-open probe permit.

Build it

Return whether each [time,success] call is permitted. Closed opens after threshold consecutive failures; a successful call resets that count. Open rejects calls until time ≥ open_until. The first permitted probe closes on success or reopens for another cooldown on failure. Ignore outcomes of rejected events. Times are nondecreasing; threshold and cooldown are positive.

Contract: Implement circuit using Python's standard library. Inputs satisfy the constraints stated here. Do not mutate the inputs. Use the provided helpers where present; they represent earlier steps.

Examples

Input: events = [[0, false], [1, false], [2, true], [6, false], [7, true], [11, true], [12, true]], threshold = 2, cooldown = 5
Expected: [true, true, false, true, false, true, true]
Input: events = [[0, false], [1, true], [2, false]], threshold = 1, cooldown = 1
Expected: [true, true, true]
Hint

Distinguish an ordinary closed-state failure from a failed half-open probe.

Review your understanding

How would multiple processes coordinate the half-open permit? When is a breaker worse than a strict timeout and concurrency limit?

Explain your reasoning in Notes before opening the worked solution. Passing the local checks completes this exercise; it does not certify production readiness or evaluate your design explanation.
